absoluteLevel.ground: The T-shirt is a common adult everyday garment, recognizable from short sleeves, collarless construction and the specified cotton undergarment sense without fashion expertise or a historical fact. Polo, sweater and blouse are actual comparable upper-body garments. Their differences can be recognized from ordinary clothing knowledge; no grammatical cue is used.

correctNoteExtraFact.fact: A T-shirt can also be an outer shirt of the same general design, rather than only an undershirt.

defects.finding: The note defines Russian «свитер» as «куртка либо пуловер». The English source defines the broader English word sweater as a knitted/crocheted jacket or pullover. A literal jacket→куртка mapping and treating pullover as an interchangeable Russian definition conflates garment categories. The shared manufacturing fact is supported, but the English range of senses is not sufficient evidence that a Russian свитер is a куртка. The note must teach its own Russian-labeled option rather than copy the wider English entry taxonomy.
defects.requiredFix: State the unambiguous supported knitting/crocheting fact about the sweater without defining it as a куртка. Do not introduce a new unsupported Russian category or new source request solely to replace the awkward literal translation. Keep the source sense scoped to clothing2a, not the sweat-producing person or hockey jersey senses.
